newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand seeks compromise on ASEAN farm tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Thailand seeks compromise on ASEAN farm tariffs.

text.p: Thai Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan called on Wednesday for the ASEAN nations to compromise on cutting tariffs on sensitive farm products.

Amnuay said before leaving for Jakarta to attend an ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) council meeting that member nations should seek solutions that benefit all sides and not be too concerned about time frames.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Brunei, Malaysia and Vietnam.
"I can't tell other members to agree on the issue. However, we should look to the same direction and be able to compromise on the issue," he told reporters.
Amnuay was referring to efforts by Indonesia and the Philippines to extend the AFTA implementation period for phasing out tariffs on some farm products, including rice and sugar.
AFTA, which covers a region of 420 million people, wants to cut tariffs on goods to between zero and five percent by 2003.
Amnuay said he understood the Philippines' and Indonesia's concerns about rice and sugar.
"Farmers in those two countries have strong political power. There could be a riot if the market is liberalized," he said.
Both countries are major importers of Thai rice.
